title: WHO: measles, dengue persist in Rohingya camps; $56.4m health appeal
excerpt: WHO's October report on the Rohingya camps counts 3,034 suspected measles cases and 12 deaths, 3,669 dengue cases and 14 deaths. The 2027 health appeal is $56.4 million.

image.alt: A nurse in protective gear adjusts an intravenous drip in a health facility in the Rohingya camps, Cox's Bazar
image.credit: DFID - UK Department for International Development / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

content:
Measles is still spreading in the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox's Bazar and is increasingly affecting children aged 5 to 15, the World Health Organization (WHO) said in its October 2026 situation report, published on ReliefWeb on Wednesday (25 November).

WHO counted 3,034 suspected measles cases investigated in the camps so far in 2026, of which 368 were laboratory-confirmed and 2,002 linked by epidemiology, plus 36 confirmed rubella cases. Twelve measles-associated deaths have been reported. Consultations are falling, WHO said, but the shift to older children "indicates an immunity gap beyond the routine target cohort", and this age group will be prioritised in a coming measles-rubella campaign. Nationally, the Directorate General of Health Services has recorded 1,371 confirmed and suspected measles deaths this year, The Daily Star reported on Friday.

Dengue is past its seasonal peak but every camp still reports cases. WHO recorded 3,669 rapid-test-confirmed cases and 14 deaths; children under 10 make up 47% of cases and 8 of the deaths. The detection of dengue serotype 3 (DENV-3) "warrants close monitoring" because of its link to large outbreaks and severe disease. Acute watery diarrhoea remains on a high plateau of about 1,790 cases a week, with 78 culture-confirmed cholera cases this year and no cholera deaths.

The Health Sector, which WHO leads, has finalised its part of the 2027 Joint Response Plan: 17 projects seeking $56.4 million, 13% more than in 2026, with $46.3 million (82%) rated high priority. The report warns that "persistent funding shortfalls" threaten coordination, surveillance, laboratories, immunisation and emergency response. More than 35,000 routine vaccine doses were given to children under two in October.

Why it matters

Three outbreaks at once in crowded camps put pressure on health partners already cutting staff. The report adds to evidence from UNHCR's latest protection report that the camps are getting harder to serve, and comes as food aid is funded only into early 2027. NGOs running clinics will need to plan for the measles-rubella campaign and for DENV-3 next monsoon.

What to watch

  • Dates and age range of the measles-rubella campaign in the camps.
  • The full 2027 Joint Response Plan launch and how much donors pledge to health.
  • Scabies mass drug administration, piloted by MSF in Camps 14, 15 and 16 from November, with a full rollout planned for March 2027 if funded.

Sources
